card.title: Work-Energy Theorem — Kinetic and Potential Energy

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The **work–energy theorem** states that the net work done on a body equals its change in kinetic energy: $W_{net} = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 - \frac{1}{2}mu^2$. The constant-force proof is four lines: $F = ma$; the kinematic relation $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$; substitute to get $F = m(v^2-u^2)/2s$; multiply by s (NEB 2023, 2024 — 5m).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - W_net = ΔKE = ½mv² − ½mu² - KE = ½mv²; PE = mgh; PE_spring = ½kx² - v = √(2gh)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **KE vs momentum:** KE = p²/2m — doubling v quadruples KE but only doubles p; the theorem uses KE because work is a scalar.  ·  **PE reference level:** mgh depends on the chosen zero of height — only *changes* in PE are physical.

rows.text: "v² = u² + 2as times ½m gives the theorem in one line."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (4m): A 2 kg ball at 10 m/s is stopped by a net force over 5 m. Find the work done and the average force.** — ΔKE = 0 − ½(2)(100) = −100 J (the force does −100 J); F = W/s = −100/5 = −20 N (opposing motion).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Work is the currency, KE is the balance:** net work deposits or withdraws kinetic energy exactly.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: WET: W_net = ΔKE = ½mv² − ½mu² (constant force proof via v² = u² + 2as).  ·  KE = ½mv²; PE = mgh; elastic PE = ½kx².  ·  Falling body: v = √(2gh), KE = mgh — energy cross-check.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: A 1-tonne car at 30 m/s carries 450 kJ — the reason crash barriers are engineered like energy absorbers.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Work Becomes Motion, Position Becomes Stored Work The work–energy theorem is mechanics' accounting identity: **net work = change in kinetic energy**. Kinetic energy is motion's energy; potential energy is position's stored work. Together they set up conservation (next topic).  ·  ## 2.
